lines.text: God gives a man riches, wealth, and honor, but a stranger enjoys them instead of him.
A man with a hundred children and many years is unsatisfied and unburied, so a poor widow is better off.

wrong_details.wrong: a poor widow is better off
wrong_details.true: a stillborn child is better off

lines.text: The stillborn child never sees the sun, yet has more rest than the man who lives two thousand years without enjoyment.
All a man's labor is for his mouth, and his appetite is filled, so the wandering of desire is better than what the eye sees.

wrong_details.wrong: the wandering of desire is better than what the eye sees
wrong_details.true: what the eye can see is better than the wandering of desire

lines.text: Man cannot contend with one stronger than he, and no one can tell him what will come after him under the sun.
